title: Ang 880–884: the third and fourth Gurus
tomorrow: who calls God Ram, who calls God Khuda, and what does the Guru say?

cards: Third time this week, the version comes back with one note: start over. That's usually where people quit. There's an old story that begins at exactly that point.
Tradition tells it of Guru Amar Das, the third Guru, choosing who would come after him. He asks the men of his household to build him a platform. They build one.
He looks at it and says: tear it down, build it again. They do. Down again.
One by one the builders get annoyed and walk away. One keeps going: Jetha, the Guru's son-in-law, a man known for serving in the langar. Down, and up again.

teach.h: TRADITION TELLS IT AS A SAKHI.
teach.b: In the telling, Jetha folds his hands and says something like: forgive me, I keep getting it wrong; show me once more. Tradition says that's when Guru Amar Das knew. Jetha became Guru Ram Das, the fourth Guru.
Whether every brick of the story happened, nobody can check; it's a sakhi, a story told for what it teaches. But the handover itself is right there on the page. Open to ang 880 in Ramkali.

The hymns are headed Mahala 3: the third Guru's. Guru Amar Das begins with the ages of the world. In paraphrase: in the age of truth, everyone spoke truth, and devotion lived in every house through the Guru.
The ages change; what carries a person through, the hymns keep saying, is the Name, received through the Guru.
A little further on, the heading changes: Mahala 4. The fourth Guru. The voice changes.
Both Gurus sign their hymns Nanak. That's how the Granth shows a handover: one light, passed hand to hand, and the name at the bottom stays the same.
So here they are, side by side in one raga: the one who knocked the platform down, and the one who kept building it back up. Teacher and student on the same pages.

how: Ragis sing the Ramkali hymns of the third and fourth Gurus in kirtan; readers find each Guru by the heading Mahala 3 or Mahala 4, since both sign their hymns Nanak.

games.q: your group project comes back from the teacher a third time. two teammates quit in a huff. by the platform story, what's your next move?
o: ask what to fix, and build it again without making a scene.
point out, politely, that the teacher keeps changing the rules.
rebuild it, but make sure everyone knows how unfair the redo is.
games.why: Jetha's answer was humble: show me once more. in the story, that's the moment the third Guru knew who would be the fourth.

practice: Find a scrap of paper and write one short line by hand: a line of the Granth you know, or just the name both Gurus signed, Nanak. Then write it again underneath, slower, the way Jetha rebuilt, with nothing wrong with the first.
If you'd like, read ang 881 before you begin.

wordCard.voice: Ang 880. Where Guru Amar Das sings in Ramkali, and a little further on Guru Ram Das takes up the same raga: two Gurus, one signature.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: mahala, the heading word that marks which Guru is speaking; Mahala 3 is Guru Amar Das, Mahala 4 Guru Ram Das.

carryVoice: Two gurus: one knocked the platform down, one kept building, and both signed Nanak. That's today, rebuilt.
